Re: Appeal of denial of lumbar fusion  
CPT 22612  
Reference number: POC-3A565C0679-61883  

Dear Grievances and Appeals Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. The denial states that the records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The submitted clinical records document extensive conservative treatment and persistent, function-limiting symptoms:

- I have experienced 24 months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from April 1, 2026, through June 10, 2026. The treatment included core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility exercises, and completion is documented in the physical-therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on March 21, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I remain unable to stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. My symptoms improve only when I sit.
- Examination documented neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.
- MRI and flexion-extension radiographs obtained July 8, 2026, show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- There is no bowel or bladder dysfunction, but the objective imaging findings and neurologic and functional limitations demonstrate persistent clinically significant disease despite conservative care.
- The records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

These records directly address the stated denial reason. They show a documented trial of supervised physical therapy, medication treatment, and an injection, followed by continued disabling symptoms and objective structural and neurologic abnormalities. The requested surgery is being recommended by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, after these nonsurgical treatments failed to provide adequate and durable relief.

I am not quoting a plan policy because the payer-specific lumbar-fusion criteria applied to this case were not publicly available in the materials reviewed. The publicly available Iowa clinical-policy list did not identify a policy specifically addressing lumbar fusion or CPT 22612. Please identify and provide the exact medical-necessity criteria, InterQual criteria or other clinical-review criteria, version, and effective date used for this determination. Please also explain specifically which criterion remains unsatisfied after consideration of the records listed above.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for the requested L4-L5 lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. If the denial is not overturned, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the specific records considered, the criteria applied, and the instructions for any further appeal or external review.

This appeal is submitted within 180 calendar days of the August 9, 2026, adverse benefit determination and no later than February 5, 2027.

Sincerely,

Emerson Jennings  
Member ID: W359699103  
Reference number: POC-3A565C0679-61883
